title.en: Prepare a comparative Statement of Profit and Loss

say.en: Revenue went up by 2.5 rupees lakh. Is that good? It depends on how much expenses went up. A comparative statement puts both years side by side. In this lesson: Prepare a comparative Statement of Profit and Loss.
Prepare a comparative Balance Sheet.
Interpret absolute and percentage changes.

body.en: Columns: Particulars, Note No., Previous year (₹), Current year (₹), Absolute change (₹), Percentage change (%). Absolute change = current − previous. Percentage change = absolute change ÷ previous year × 100. Both the *comparative Statement* of Profit and Loss and the comparative Balance Sheet follow this format.

title.en: Comparative statement of profit and loss

caption.en: Absolute change = current year − previous year; percentage change = absolute change ÷ previous year × 100. A small rise in revenue can mean a large rise in profit.
caption.kn: ನಿರಪೇಕ್ಷ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ = ಪ್ರಸಕ್ತ ವರ್ಷ − ಹಿಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷ; ಶೇಕಡಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ = ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ÷ ಹಿಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷ × 100.

tryThis.en: Revenue up 20%, expenses up 12.5%: by what percent did profit rise?
Make revenue and expenses both rise by 10%. What happens to the profit percentage change?
Why is the percentage change of profit meaningless when last year's profit was a loss?

say.en: Comparative statement of profit and loss Absolute change equals current year - previous year; percentage change equals absolute change divided by previous year times 100. A small rise in revenue can mean a large rise in profit.

say.en: When revenue grows faster than expenses, profit grows faster than both.

problem.en: Prepare a comparative Statement of Profit and Loss: Revenue from operations ₹10,00,000 (2023-24) and ₹12,50,000 (2024-25); Expenses ₹6,00,000 and ₹7,20,000; tax 30%.

answer.en: Revenue +25%, expenses +20%, profit after tax +32.5%: profitability has improved.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Prepare a comparative Statement of Profit and Loss: Revenue from operations 10,00,000 rupees (2023-24) and 12,50,000 rupees (2024-25); Expenses 6,00,000 rupees and 7,20,000 rupees; tax 30 percent.
Revenue: change 2,50,000 rupees; 2,50,000 divided by 10,00,000 equals 25 percent.
Expenses: change 1,20,000 rupees; 1,20,000 divided by 6,00,000 equals 20 percent.
Profit before tax: 4,00,000 rupees gives 5,30,000 rupees; change 1,30,000 rupees equals 32.5 percent.
Tax 30 percent: 1,20,000 rupees gives 1,59,000 rupees. Profit after tax: 2,80,000 rupees gives 3,71,000 rupees; change 91,000 rupees equals 32.5 percent.
So the answer is Revenue plus 25 percent, expenses plus 20 percent, profit after tax plus 32.5 percent: profitability has improved.

heading.en: Always divide by the OLD year

body.en: In comparative statements, the denominator is the previous (old) year. In common size statements, the denominator is the total of the same year.

mnemonic.en: Comparative: divide by Old. Common size: divide by Total.

say.en: In comparative statements, the denominator is the previous old year. In common size statements, the denominator is the total of the same year.
